title: Ternary weights on real text: 10M byte-level LMs on enwik8, byte-matched
follows: R1.29 (PASS on suite v3: ternary MLP 47.2 vs 38.8 byte-matched fp32), R1.14 (FAIL for Rouge's state; sliding window with a cached block best on long streams), R1.31 (ternary dominates the stored-bytes frontier on suite v3)
question: Does R1.29's result transfer to real text: does a 10M Transformer with ternary MLP weights (15.2 MB stored) predict enwik8 better than an fp32 Transformer with the same stored bytes (d=200, 15.6 MB), and stay close to the full fp32 model (38.9 MB)? And does the combination of the two measured winners (window architecture + ternary MLP) keep the window's long-stream quality?

setup.hardware: GitHub-hosted CPU runners (tier 0, $0), up to 2 resumable attempts per run

compute.cpu_flops_measured: ternary MLP: 1.28 s per training step vs 0.78 s fp32 (4-core container; the straight-through quantisation costs time, no ternary kernel)

predictions.PASS: ternary beats the byte-matched fp32 model by >= 0.03 BPB (T1) and is within 0.05 BPB of the full fp32 model (T2)
predictions.priors: T1 likely: the byte-matched fp32 model has 2.5x fewer parameters. T2 uncertain: BitNet b1.58 reports parity with fp16 only from about 3B parameters; R1.29's gain over full fp32 on suite v3 was within seed noise and may be regularisation, which matters less on undertrained real text (0.36 epochs).
predictions.T3: reported: window-ternary (1.25 MiB inference memory, 15.2 MB stored) vs the full fp32 Transformer (5 MiB, 38.9 MB) on bytes 1k-4k
predictions.T4: reported: attention and embeddings stay fp32, so the whole model stores 0.39x the fp32 bytes, not 1/16

not_claimed: Ternary training is prior art. The question is whether the one mechanism with independent PASS evidence in this program survives on real text before it is used in R1.32/R1.40. No kernel speed-up is claimed: ternary matmuls run as fp32 here.
